---
title: "Imbalanced Dataset"
description: "A dataset in which some classes or outcomes occur much more often than others."
term: "Imbalanced Dataset"
letter: "I"
category: "Model Evaluation"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

An imbalanced dataset has many more examples of some outcomes than others.
For example, a dataset might contain thousands of ordinary transactions but
only a small number of fraudulent ones.

## Technical explanation

Class imbalance describes unequal class frequencies in a classification
dataset. It can affect learning and evaluation, especially when the minority
class is important or the model is optimized for an aggregate objective that
is dominated by the majority class. The impact depends on the task, sample
size, label quality, and decision costs; imbalance alone does not prove a
model is biased or unusable.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

A model can achieve high accuracy by predicting the common class while
missing rare but consequential events. Engineers should understand class
frequencies, select metrics aligned with the task, and decide how to handle
mistakes based on operational costs.

## How it works

First, inspect class counts and relevant slices in the training and
evaluation data. Possible responses include collecting more minority-class
examples, using class-weighted losses, resampling training data, or changing
the decision threshold. Evaluate with per-class measures and metrics such as
precision, recall, or area under the precision-recall curve. Apply sampling
only to training data, and keep the evaluation distribution representative
of deployment.

## Practical example

In fraud detection, report how many fraudulent transactions are found and
how many legitimate transactions are incorrectly flagged, not just the
overall percentage classified correctly. A
[confusion matrix](../C/confusion-matrix.qmd) makes those outcomes visible.

## Common misconceptions

- Class imbalance does not always make a model fail; the effect depends on
  data, the task, and the chosen objective.
- Accuracy alone can hide poor performance on rare classes.
- Oversampling or undersampling is not a substitute for checking labels,
  data leakage, and deployment costs.
